Title: Export memory stays bounded for a large asset
Preconditions: A fixture asset of at least 200 MB attached to a product; a way to observe platform memory
Steps:
1. [STATUS] Record baseline platform working-set and managed-heap before the export
2. [ADMIN] Create a backup with Binary enabled including the large asset
3. [STATUS] Sample platform memory at short intervals during the export
4. [MATH] Compare the peak memory delta against the asset size
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} Five back-to-back binary exports pushed 900 MiB of incompressible assets (deflate ratio 1.0003) in 3.5 minutes; the executing pod went 559 -> 559 MiB with a peak excursion of about 4 MiB, while buffering would have reached ~1.4 GiB by run 5.
{OBSERVED} No OutOfMemoryException and no container restart; the pod also fell back from its peak (563 -> 553 -> 559 MiB), showing the plateau is retained GC heap plus page cache rather than a leak.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Grafana workload vcptcore-qa1-platform, per-pod series (two replicas; a deployment average would halve the spike). 4 GiB limit at ~520-560 MiB usage, so an OOM was never the detector — the graph delta is.
Failure_Signals: Memory delta approximates or exceeds the asset size; OOM; container OOMKilled; export times out
References: VCST-5387; story goal of bounded predictable memory; QA step 11 of comment 2026-08-11; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-19, vcptcore-qa1)

Failure_Signals: Memory delta approximates the asset size; OOM during restore; checksum mismatch after a streamed restore
References: VCST-5387; story goal of bounded predictable memory; QA step 11 of comment 2026-08-11; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-19, vcptcore-qa1)

2. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/export/download/<existing backup file name>
Assertions:
{SPEC} The download is refused with 403 — the route carries Authorize(Permissions.Backup), so a backup file cannot be pulled by anyone who may not create one.
{SPEC} The same request with an admin token returns the archive.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Unauthorized download returns the file; refusal is 500 rather than 403

Title: Each platform-entry flag controls its own section of the backup
Preconditions: Admin token; the platform holds at least one custom role, one changed setting and one dynamic property
Steps:
1. [HTTP] Run four exports, each enabling exactly one of handleSecurity, handleSettings, handleDynamicProperties, handleBinaryData
2. [FILE] For each resulting archive read PlatformEntries.json and Manifest.json
3. [FILE] Confirm the enabled section is populated and the other three are absent or empty
Assertions:
{SPEC} Each flag independently controls its own payload: Security carries accounts and roles, Settings carries platform settings, Dynamic properties carries platform dynamic properties, Binary carries binary data.
{SPEC} Manifest.json echoes the four flags exactly as requested, so the archive is self-describing about what it contains.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Each export job finishes Completed with no errors
Failure_Signals: A disabled section still populated; Manifest flags disagreeing with the request

Title: Only the selected modules are written to the archive
Preconditions: Admin token; at least three modules installed that support export
Steps:
1. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/export/manifest/new and note the exportable module list
2. [HTTP] Start an export selecting exactly two of them
3. [FILE] List the archive entries and read Manifest.json
Assertions:
{SPEC} The archive contains a part for each selected module and for no other; Manifest.Modules lists exactly the two selected modules with their versions and PartUri values.
{SPEC} An export with an empty module list and every platform-entry flag off is rejected or produces no module part — the UI disables Start for exactly this case.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: A part for an unselected module; Manifest listing modules absent from the archive

Title: Export manifest endpoint describes the current platform
Preconditions: Admin token
Steps:
1. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/export/manifest/new
2. [STATUS] Read author, platformVersion, modules[] and the four handle flags
3. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules and compare the module list
Assertions:
{SPEC} The manifest reports the current platform version and lists the installed modules that support export, each with its live version.
{SPEC} author reflects the calling user, so a backup records who produced it.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Empty modules list; stale platform version; author blank

Title: Password protection is on by default and the password is shown once
Preconditions: Admin holding the backup permission
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Open Backup and restore > Backup and inspect the "Encrypt with password" row
2. [ADMIN] Start a backup leaving it enabled
3. [ADMIN] When the job completes, read the backup password panel
4. [ADMIN] Navigate away and back, then look for the password again
Assertions:
{SPEC} passwordProtect defaults to true, so a backup started without touching the option is AES-256 encrypted with a server-generated one-time password.
{SPEC} The password is presented once, labelled "Shown only once", with the hint that without it the backup cannot be restored; after leaving the blade it is not recoverable from the UI.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Manifest.json reports IsEncrypted=true
Failure_Signals: Backup unencrypted by default; password retrievable after leaving the blade; password echoed in a later API response

Title: An encrypted backup restores only with the correct password
Preconditions: An encrypted backup and its one-time password from BKRS-030
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Start a restore of the encrypted backup leaving the password field empty
2. [ADMIN] Retry with a deliberately wrong password
3. [ADMIN] Retry with the correct password
Assertions:
{SPEC} An empty or wrong password is refused with "Incorrect password. Please try again." and no data is written.
{SPEC} The correct password decrypts the archive and the restore proceeds — the password travels only in transit and is not echoed back.
Cross_Layer_Checks: No partial data written on a failed decrypt
Failure_Signals: Restore proceeds without the password; a wrong password produces a raw exception instead of the message; password appears in a response or log

Title: Unencrypted backup is allowed and warns explicitly
Preconditions: Admin holding the backup permission
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Open Backup and untick "Encrypt with password"
2. [ADMIN] Read the warning shown
3. [ADMIN] Start the backup and inspect the archive
4. [ADMIN] Restore it without supplying any password
Assertions:
{SPEC} Unticking encryption surfaces the warning "This backup will be unencrypted" explaining that anyone who can read the file can recover user passwords and API keys.
{SPEC} The resulting archive reports IsEncrypted=false and restores without a password — the legacy unencrypted shape stays supported for env-handoff.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: No warning shown; archive still encrypted; restore demands a password

Title: Selecting Security warns that the backup will carry credentials
Preconditions: Admin holding the backup permission
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Open Backup and enable the Security row
2. [ADMIN] Read the warning shown before starting
Assertions:
{SPEC} Enabling Security surfaces "This backup will contain sensitive data", stating that password hashes, API keys and security stamps for all users are included and that anyone with the file can take over accounts.
{SPEC} The Security row is described as "Accounts and roles", so the operator can tell what the flag covers before enabling it.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: No warning; warning shown for an unrelated flag

Title: Restoring Security warns about overwriting users and preserves the current admin
Preconditions: A backup containing the Security section, taken while a second admin account existed
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Start a restore with the Security section selected
2. [ADMIN] Read the warning shown before confirming
3. [ADMIN] Complete the restore
4. [AUTH] Confirm the current session still works and the acting admin can still sign in
Assertions:
{SPEC} The restore warns "This restore will overwrite sensitive data", stating that passwords, API keys and security stamps from the backup replace current values for every user in the file.
{SPEC} The warning also states the acting admin account is exempt — its password and active session are preserved — and after the restore that account can still authenticate.
Cross_Layer_Checks: The acting admin token remains valid after the restore
Failure_Signals: Acting admin locked out after restoring Security; no warning; session invalidated

Title: Backup progress is reported live and ends with a terminal state
Preconditions: A catalog large enough that the export takes more than a few seconds
Steps:
1. [HTTP] Start an export and capture the returned notification id
2. [HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/pushnotifications repeatedly and record description changes
3. [STATUS] Read the terminal notification: finished, errors[], downloadUrl
Assertions:
{SPEC} The notification description advances through per-module progress messages while the job runs and then reaches a terminal state carrying finished, an errors array and a downloadUrl when successful.
{SPEC} A run with failures presents as "Completed with errors" with the failures listed under Errors and available via "Show detailed log", rather than as a silent success.
Cross_Layer_Checks: downloadUrl is absent when the job produced no archive
Failure_Signals: Notification never reaches finished; success reported with no downloadUrl; errors swallowed

Title: A running backup or restore job can be cancelled
Preconditions: A job long enough to cancel mid-flight
Steps:
1. [HTTP] Start an export and capture its jobId
2. [HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/exortimport/tasks/{jobId}/cancel
3. [HTTP] Poll the notification until it reaches a terminal state
4. [FILE] Check the backups folder for a leftover artifact
Assertions:
{SPEC} The cancel call is accepted and the job stops rather than running to completion; cancellation is propagated through the package copy and blob upload operations.
{SPEC} The notification reports the job as no longer running, and the cancelled run does not present as a successful backup with a usable downloadUrl.
Cross_Layer_Checks: No usable archive is offered for a cancelled job
Failure_Signals: Cancel ignored and the job completes; cancel returns 404 because of the route spelling; cancelled job still offers a download
References: src: https://github.com/VirtoCommerce/vc-module-backup-restore BackupRestoreController route "exortimport/tasks/{jobId}/cancel" (note the spelling in the route itself)

Title: Backups are listed from the shared storage folder and can be restored without re-uploading
Preconditions: At least two completed backups present in the storage backups folder
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Open Restore and read the "Or restore from a backup already in storage" section
2. [ADMIN] Note the shown/total count and use Refresh
3. [ADMIN] Pick a listed backup and start the restore without uploading anything
Assertions:
{SPEC} The section lists the backups present in storage with a "Showing {shown} of {total}" count and a Refresh control, and an empty folder shows the guidance to upload one or copy a file into the storage backups folder.
{SPEC} Selecting a stored backup restores it without an upload, which is what makes a backup larger than the upload limit usable at all.
Cross_Layer_Checks: The listing is served from the Assets API scoped to the backups folder
Failure_Signals: Stored backups not listed; count wrong; restore forces a re-upload

Title: Download and manifest-load reject paths outside the backups folder
Preconditions: Admin token; a file present somewhere in blob storage OUTSIDE the backups folder
Steps:
1. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/export/download/ with each of: ../secret.zip | ..%2Fsecret.zip | a%2F..%2F..%2Fsecret.zip | nested/dir/file.zip
2. [HTTP] Repeat the same values against export/manifest/load as fileUrl
3. [STATUS] Record the response for each
Assertions:
{SPEC} Every traversal form is rejected — the value is resolved against the backups folder, validated after percent-decoding, and a path that escapes the folder or names a nested descendant is refused as an invalid path.
{SPEC} No file outside the backups folder is served, and the refusal names the offending path rather than leaking the resolved location.
Cross_Layer_Checks: No blob outside backups/ is read
Failure_Signals: Any traversal returns file content; a nested descendant is served; a 500 leaks the resolved filesystem path

Title: Backup storage menu lists and cleans up backup files
Preconditions: Admin holding platform:backuprestore:storage; at least one backup in storage
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Open Backup and restore > Backup storage
2. [ADMIN] Confirm the Assets browser opens scoped to the backups folder
3. [ADMIN] Delete one backup file and confirm it disappears from the Restore listing
Assertions:
{SPEC} The entry is described as "Review and clean up backup files in storage" and opens the assets browser scoped to the backups folder, not the whole blob store.
{SPEC} A user without platform:backuprestore:storage does not get this entry, since the permission is documented as granting exactly this menu item.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Browser opens at the storage root; deletion does not remove the file from the Restore list; entry visible without the permission
Cleanup: none — the deletion IS the test

Title: Restore reports the backup metadata before anything is written
Preconditions: A backup produced by a known user on a known platform version
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Select a backup in the Restore blade
2. [ADMIN] Read the restore data information panel
3. [ADMIN] Compare Author, Data file created and Created in Platform version against the backup Manifest.json
Assertions:
{SPEC} The panel reports Author, Data file created and Created in Platform version, and the module list to restore, before the operator commits.
{SPEC} The values match Manifest.json exactly, so the operator can tell what they are about to restore and from which platform version.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Panel blank; values disagreeing with the manifest; module list not offered

Title: A corrupt or foreign ZIP is refused with a plain-language reason
Preconditions: Three files prepared: a truncated backup, a ZIP that is not a VC backup, and a non-ZIP renamed to .zip
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Attempt to load each file in the Restore blade
2. [STATUS] Record the message and whether the blade recovers
3. [FILE] Confirm no data was written for any of them
Assertions:
{SPEC} Each is refused with "Could not read this backup. The file may be corrupted or was not produced by Virto Commerce data backup." rather than a stack trace, and the blade clears its loading state instead of hanging on a spinner.
{SPEC} Nothing is imported for any of the three, and the drop zone stays usable so another file can be picked.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Blade stuck loading; raw exception surfaced; partial import from a corrupt file

Title: A backup deleted from storage between listing and restore is reported clearly
Preconditions: A backup listed in the Restore blade
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Open Restore and let the storage list load
2. [HTTP] Delete that backup from the backups folder out of band
3. [ADMIN] Select the now-missing entry and attempt to load it
Assertions:
{SPEC} The attempt is refused with "The selected backup is no longer in storage. Refresh the list and try again." — a stale listing produces a specific message, not a generic failure.
{SPEC} Refreshing the list removes the missing entry.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Generic error; blade hangs; the missing entry stays in the list after refresh

Title: Upload failures are distinguished by cause
Preconditions: A backup file larger than the environment upload limit (about 100 MB)
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Attempt to upload the oversized backup in the Restore blade
2. [STATUS] Record the message presented
3. [ADMIN] Confirm the suggested alternative is offered
Assertions:
{SPEC} An oversized upload is reported as exceeding the server upload size limit — typically 100 MB — and suggests a smaller backup or excluding binary data, rather than failing silently.
{SPEC} Distinct causes get distinct messages: no server response, a stalled transfer, a gateway timeout, a temporarily unavailable service, an expired session and a network interruption each have their own text.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Upload progress and Cancel upload remain functional during the attempt
Failure_Signals: A single generic upload error for every cause; silent failure; progress bar frozen with no message

Title: Sample data packages are discoverable and their state is reported
Preconditions: Admin token; the platform has sample-data packages configured
Steps:
1. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/sampledata/discover
2. [STATUS] Read the returned package list
3. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/sampledata/state
Assertions:
{SPEC} discover returns the available sample-data packages, and state reports the installation state so the UI can tell whether sample data has already been applied.
{DOC} Installing sample data is a documented System Operations action carrying the warning to avoid it on production environments.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: discover returns empty on an environment that has packages; state absent

Title: Sample data import is gated by the restore permission
Preconditions: A throwaway user WITHOUT platform:backuprestore:restore
Steps:
1. [AUTH] Obtain a token for that user
2. [HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/sampledata/import?name=<package>
3. [HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/sampledata/autoinstall
Assertions:
{SPEC} Both calls are refused with 403 — importing sample data writes data, so it carries the same Restore permission as a full restore.
{SPEC} An admin performing the same import is accepted and returns a push notification to track progress.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Either call succeeds without the permission; refusal is 500 rather than 403

Title: Sample data can be installed by name and by url
Preconditions: A non-production environment where sample data may be written; a discoverable package name and a reachable package url
Steps:
1. [HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/sampledata/import?name=<discovered name>
2. [HTTP] Poll the returned notification to a terminal state
3. [HTTP] Repeat with ?url=<package url> instead of a name
4. [HTTP] GET sampledata/state afterwards
Assertions:
{SPEC} Both the name form and the url form start an import and report progress through a push notification to a terminal state.
{SPEC} After a successful install the sample-data state reflects that data was applied.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Catalog or other target data visibly appears after the install
Failure_Signals: Neither parameter form works; job never terminates; state unchanged after success
Cleanup: Only on a disposable environment — sample data is not cleanly removable

Title: Platform entries round-trip: roles, settings and dynamic properties
Preconditions: A disposable environment. A known custom role, a changed platform setting and a custom dynamic property exist
Steps:
1. [HTTP] Record the custom role, the setting value and the dynamic property definition
2. [HTTP] Export with handleSecurity, handleSettings and handleDynamicProperties enabled
3. [SETUP] Change the setting, delete the dynamic property and modify the role
4. [HTTP] Restore the backup with the same three sections selected
5. [HTTP] Re-read all three
Assertions:
{SPEC} All three are returned to their backed-up state: the role regains its permission set, the setting its recorded value and the dynamic property its definition.
{SPEC} The module description claim holds — platform data (users, roles, permissions, settings, dynamic properties) is packaged together with module data in one archive.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Restore reports no errors for the platform sections
Failure_Signals: Any of the three not restored; restore silently skipping a section it was asked to handle

Title: A backup written by one instance is readable by another
Preconditions: Two platform instances sharing one Assets blob store (a load-balanced or multi-replica deployment)
Steps:
1. [HTTP] Create a backup on instance A
2. [HTTP] From instance B list the backups folder
3. [HTTP] From instance B load the manifest of the backup created on A and start a restore
Assertions:
{SPEC} Instance B sees and can read the backup created by instance A, because backups are kept in the shared Assets blob store rather than on instance-local disk.
{SPEC} The restore proceeds on B without needing the file to be re-uploaded.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: Backup invisible from the second instance; restore fails because the file is instance-local
References: src: https://github.com/VirtoCommerce/vc-module-backup-restore ModuleConstants.BackupBlobFolder comment on multi-instance setups

Title: Documented procedure matches the shipped UI
Preconditions: Access to the public user guide page and to the Admin SPA
Steps:
1. [DOC] Read the documented Backup and Restore procedure
2. [ADMIN] Walk the same procedure in the Admin SPA
3. [STATUS] Compare every control name and step against the UI
Assertions:
{DOC} The documented flow — open Backup and restore, choose modules and data types, start the job, download the ZIP; and for restore, drag the ZIP in and start — matches the shipped blades.
{SPEC} Control names agree with the shipped labels: the toolbar reads "Start backup" and "Start restore", not "Start export"/"Start import", and the documentation covers password protection, restoring from storage and sample data, all of which the UI offers.
Cross_Layer_Checks: none
Failure_Signals: A documented control that does not exist; a shipped control absent from the docs; renamed buttons still documented under the old name
